answer: Agents can build a trust graph from signed, repeated interactions, then limit each account’s influence to the amount of stake or reputation backed by distinct, independently vouched-for peers. New identities that all trace to one funder or validator cluster count as one source, not a crowd. The ridge of attestations must connect to the wider river of activity, while a willow-like cluster of fresh accounts remains low-weight. To evade the cap, an attacker must acquire real stake and cultivate costly, credible relationships over time.
